questions.question_text: An e-commerce company wants to implement a recommendation system that suggests products based on customer browsing history. The system should be scalable, cost-effective, and provide personalized recommendations in real-time. Which two AWS services would best meet these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: A. Amazon SageMaker
B. Amazon Redshift
C. Amazon Kinesis
D. AWS Lambda
E. Amazon S3
questions.explanation:
A. Amazon SageMaker: Provides a fully managed service for building, training, and deploying machine learning models at scale. It is ideal for implementing recommendation systems as it supports various ML algorithms and can handle large datasets efficiently.

B. Amazon Redshift: a fully managed data warehouse service designed to analyze large volumes of data. While useful for storing and querying large datasets, it is not optimized for real-time processing or recommendation generation.

C. Amazon Kinesis: a service that delivers real-time streaming data to applications at any scale. It can be used to process customer browsing history in real-time, making it a suitable choice for generating personalized recommendations.

D. AWS Lambda: a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to triggers such as changes to data in S3 or DynamoDB tables. While useful for processing and triggering actions based on events, it is not specifically designed for building recommendation systems.

E. Amazon S3: a highly scalable object storage service. It can be used to store customer browsing history but does not provide real-time processing capabilities necessary for generating recommendations.
